title: Verify a domain for outbound mail
cost: About 0.02 USD of AI credits: the one assistant question in step 4. Nothing else is charged.
goal: The mail service needs proof that we own example.org before it will send from it. The proof is one TXT record at the domain registrar.
This run reads the current records, adds the one record, and records what the registrar shows afterwards.
checked: A public lookup shows no verification record on example.org today.
The mail service lists the domain as Pending.
stops: The registrar shows a different domain, or an account you do not recognise.
The registrar asks for a payment or a plan change.
A verification record already exists with a different value.
never: Passwords, sign-in codes or recovery codes.

steps.title: Read the current DNS records
steps.hands: sign in to the registrar if asked.
do: Open the DNS records list for example.org.
Find every TXT record on the root name.

capture.label: TXT records on the root name
capture.shape: One per line: the value, shortened to its first 40 characters.

steps.title: Add the verification record
steps.rule: If a record starting with mail-verify= already exists with the same value, set this step to Skipped by rule. If one exists with a different value, stop.
do: Type: TXT. Name: @. Value: mail-verify=sample-0000. TTL: 3600.

capture.label: The record as the registrar now shows it
capture.shape: Type, name, value and TTL, exactly as displayed.

steps.title: Confirm the mail service sees it
do: Wait up to two minutes and reload once.
steps.expect: example.org shows Verified within two minutes of pressing Verify.

measured.text: A public lookup from the seat's machine saw no mail-verify= record; the service showed Pending.

steps.title: Ask the support assistant
asks: Is example.org verified for sending, and since when?
steps.expect: The reply names example.org as Verified, gives the time, and links the domain's settings page with an address that opens it.

measured.text: On the branch build the reply named the domain but linked a settings page that does not exist.
